verses.1: Summoning the entire body of vanaras, Sugriva, the bull among monkeys, said, 'Go to the places I have described and look for Sita in order to fulfil Rama's objective'.
verses.2: Having understood Sugriva's strict orders, the forces of monkeys started moving. They spread like locusts all over the earth.
verses.3: Rama accompanied by Lakshmana stayed back at Prasravana mountain looking forward for the expiry of the month fixed for the monkeys to trace Sita's whereabouts.
verses.4: Then the monkey warrior Satavali departed for the north, surrounded by kings of mountains.
verses.5: Vinata, leader of the monkeys, set out for the eastern direction.The troop leader, son of the Windgod along with Angada and Tara left for the south inhabited by Agastya.
verses.6: Vinata, leader of the monkeys, set out for the eastern direction.The troop leader, son of the Windgod along with Angada and Tara left for the south inhabited by Agastya.
verses.7: 'The chieftain Sushena, tiger among the monkeys, started quickly for the fearsome western direction ruled by Varuna.
verses.8: Sugriva, chief of the army of monkeys, having sent the leaders to all quarters felt relieved and rejoiced.
verses.9: Addressed thus by the king, all the monkeys departed quickly from there for their respective directions with all enthusiasm.
verses.10: The powerful monkeys went gallopping and chattering, leaping and screaming.
verses.11: Thus addressed by the king, the leaders of the monkeys shouted, 'We will kill Ravana and get back Sita'.
verses.12: 'I shall kill Ravana singlehanded in war and quickly get back Janaka's daughter churning (the enemy army).' (said one)
verses.13: 'I will alone restore Sita, exhausted and trembling (in fear), even from the nether world. Wait here' (said another leader).
verses.14: 'I will smash trees, shatter mountains, cleave the earth and churn up the seas'. (said a another).
verses.15: 'I can doubtless cross a distance of a hundred yojanas' said one. Another said,' I can leap a hundred yojanas more'.
verses.16: Then the vanaras there, proud of their strength, spoke thus one after another in the presence of the king of vanaras.
